Surya.name: Surya Deva
Surya.note: The deva of the sun; an Aditya, son of the devi Aditi and the rishi Kashyap. Father of Karna, whom Kunti bore before her marriage by invoking Surya with a boon she wished to test.

Yama.name: Yama (Dharma)
Yama.note: Dharma, the deva of righteousness and lord of justice; father of Yudhishthira, who inherited his unwavering truth.

Vayu.name: Vayu Deva
Vayu.note: The deva of the wind; father of the mighty Bhima (and, in the earlier age of the Ramayan, of Hanuman).

Indra.name: Indra Deva
Indra.note: King of the devas, wielder of the thunderbolt; an Aditya, son of Aditi and Kashyap, and so a brother of Surya. Father of Arjuna, to whom he later gave celestial weapons and a year's respite from Kurukshetra as Brihannala. By name — killing Vritra with the thunderbolt made from the sage Dadhichi's bones, the many curses on him for seducing Ahalya (a thousand marks that became a thousand eyes, in one telling), losing and regaining his throne across the Bali and Vamana story, and testing Karna by begging his armour and earrings away in disguise.

Nasatya.note: One of the twin Ashvini Kumaras, devas of dawn and healing; father, by Madri, of Nakula.

Dasra.note: One of the twin Ashvini Kumaras, devas of dawn and healing; father, by Madri, of Sahadeva.

Aditi.note: Daughter of Daksha, wife of Kashyap; mother of the Adityas, the devas.

Sandhya.note: Sanjna, daughter of Vishvakarma and chief wife of Surya; mother of Vaivasvata Manu, Yama, Yami and the Ashvin twins.

Chaya.note: The shadow-image of Sandhya, second wife of Surya; mother of Shani, Tapati and Savarni Manu.

Yami.note: Daughter of Surya and Sandhya, twin of Yama; the river-goddess Yamuna.

Shani.note: Son of Surya and Chaya; the slow, stern planet Saturn.

Tapati.note: Daughter of Surya and Chaya; wed King Samvarana, an ancestress of the Kurus.

Savarni.note: Son of Surya and Chaya; the Manu of a coming age (Savarni Manu).

Varuna.note: Aditya lord of the waters and cosmic order.

Mitra.note: Aditya of friendship and contracts, paired with Varuna.

Aryaman.note: Aditya of custom, patron of marriage and the ancestors.

Bhaga.note: Aditya of fortune and inherited share.

Pushan.note: Aditya of roads, herds and safe journeys.

Vamana.note: The dwarf brahmin who came to Bali's sacrifice and asked for three steps of ground, then took the earth with one and the sky with the second, and set the third on Bali's own head. Son of Kashyapa and Aditi, and so a brother of Indra, whose lost heaven he was recovering. The fifteenth of the avatars, SB 1.3.19.

Tvashtar.note: Aditya, the divine artificer (Vishvakarma); father of Sanjna (Sandhya), Surya's wife.

Vishvarupa.note: Three-headed son of Tvashtar, priest to the devas, beheaded by Indra.

Sachi.note: Also Indrani/Pulomaja; queen of the devas, wife of Indra.

Jayanti.note: Daughter of Indra; wed to Shukracharya.

Devasena.note: Daughter of Indra; wed to Kartikeya (Skanda).

Varuni.note: Goddess of wine (sura); rose from the churning of the ocean of milk and was claimed by the asuras. SB 8.8.

Revanta.note: Son of Surya and Sandhya (Sanjna); a demigod horseman, leader of the Guhyakas, who wards off thieves and disease.

Suvarchala.note: Daughter of Surya; wife of Hanuman. Parashara Samhita, not the Bhagavata; a Telangana temple tradition (Suvarchala Anjaneya Swamy).

unions.note: Mother unnamed in the sources. Parashara Samhita.
